title: Going straight into the gym after phone sign-in is only tested by looking for words in the code
what: When a member the gym knows signs in by phone number, the app joins the gym, saves the setup answers and opens the app, or falls back to the 3 setup questions if a step fails. No test runs this. The tests open the file as text and check that certain lines exist and come in a certain order. They pass even if the join fails, the save is skipped or the fall-back never shows, and they break on a harmless rename. The machine list also shows the sign-in file and the phone screen are imported by no test.
expected: A test runs the straight-in step with the join working, refused and offline, and with the save failing, and checks whether the member ends up in the app, on the 3 questions or seeing 'That did not work. Try again.'
who: members signing in by phone number
fix_line: Replace the text checks with a test that runs the straight-in step for each outcome

title: The demo's personal records follow an older rule than a real workout's
what: The demo member's records are worked out by a separate copy of the record rule. Its note says it repeats the app's rule, but it misses the owner's rule that a lighter set is never a 1-rep-max record (95 kg x 8 after 100 kg x 5). So a freshly loaded demo can show records a real member would never get, until the next app start runs a repair that rewrites them. Two copies of one rule drift apart.
expected: The demo builds its records with the same rule the app uses for a finished workout, so the demo shows exactly what a member would see.
who: owners showing the demo, members trying the demo
how_often: every demo load, until the next app start
fix_line: Have the demo use the app's shared record rule instead of its own copy

title: Two of the one-time record repairs fail at start-up without leaving any trace
what: The one-time record repairs are started from two places: app start-up and after a Drive restore. After a restore every failure is logged. At start-up two of the three record repairs, the history speed-up and the library re-link after loading the demo throw their errors away with nothing logged. If one keeps failing, wrong records stay on the phone and nobody can see why.
expected: Every repair that fails leaves a log line, the same way at start-up as after a restore, and the repairs are started from one shared list.
fix_line: Log every repair failure and run the repairs from one shared list

title: A save-queue test relies on a real 0.4-second wait for a 0.3-second save
what: The test that checks a failed Finish keeps its warning while the member keeps typing waits 400 ms of real time for a draft save that fires after 300 ms. On a busy test machine the save can land after the check and the test fails with nothing wrong in the app.
expected: The test moves a fake clock past the save delay, or waits for the save itself, before checking.
how_often: now and then on a slow test run
fix_line: Use a fake clock or wait for the save instead of a fixed pause
